candidates.title: LLMGuard: Safeguarding Real-Time Inference for Large Language Models on Edge Devices
candidates.venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
candidates.abstract: TEE-shielded secure inference offers an efficient solution to protect valuable edge-deployed models from potential thefts. Nevertheless, existing methods are lack of theoretical security analysis, failing to achieve the optimal security. Furthermore, while feasible for small models, existing methods are excessively heavyweight for Large Language Models (LLM). For LLaMA-7B, they introduce GB-level secure memory requirement and hundredfold inference latency, severely compromising real-time utility. To solve these problems, we first present a Bayesian theory framework of Model Stealing (MS) attacks, which decomposes MS into prior and posterior knowledge leakage. Based on this framework, LLMGuard is proposed, which presents two components: First, Intrinsic Parameters Shielding is designed to shield all private parameters, preventing prior knowledge leakage. This approach significantly decreases the secure memory usage and achieves inference speedup. Second, since OTP is not applicable to LLMs, Random Slices Composition is developed to obfuscate intermediate distributions with no computational overhead, minimizing posterior knowledge leakage efficiently. Experimental results demonstrate that LLMGuard downgrades model to black-box inference with negligible accuracy loss, while delivering \(43\times\) inference speedup on LLaMA compared to fully shielded methods. The proposed LLMGuard effectively addresses concerns related to intellectual property theft on edge, boosting the secure deployment of LLMs on untrusted devices.
candidates.reason: LLMGuardはモデル窃取攻撃をベイズ理論で分解し、TEE保護下のエッジLLM推論のセキュアメモリとレイテンシ overhead を大幅に削減する。安全なLLM推論システムへの直接の貢献が確認できる

candidates.title: DIAMM: A Distributed Inference Acceleration Framework for Multimodal Edge Applications
candidates.venue: IEEE Transactions on Parallel and Distributed Systems
candidates.abstract: Multimodal applications such as educational assistants and medical diagnosis demand high concurrency and low latency, and are increasingly served by edge inference enhanced with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). However, heterogeneous multimodal models and fragmented edge resources couple three problems that prior work treats separately, namely compute and queue overload, unstable cold-start latency, and unreliable retrieval. Optimizing any one in isolation shifts the bottleneck to the others. To address this, we propose DIAMM (Distributed Inference Acceleration for Multimodal edge applications), which couples scheduling, cold-start, and retrieval through shared runtime signals so they co-adapt instead of competing. First, a queue management and service deployment (QMSD) algorithm adaptively prioritizes tasks and allocates service replicas under constrained edge resources. Second, a multimodal warm-up method prefetches model weights in the background to mask migration overhead, reducing cold-start latency while lowering the storage footprint. Third, a fine-tuned Question–Knowledge Assessment (QKA) module filters task-irrelevant retrieval contexts to cut prompt contamination and downstream LLM cost. We implement DIAMM on a Kubernetes-orchestrated cluster spanning x86 hosts and NVIDIA Jetson devices, and evaluate it across five multimodal tasks. Compared with baselines, DIAMM reduces average task-completion latency by 16.5% (up to 35.7%), attains a task-completion rate of up to 97.0%, and lowers average storage by about 6.3× relative to full weight replication on the x86 cluster.
candidates.reason: DIAMMはエッジ上のマルチモーダル推論について、キュー管理とサービス配置、コールドスタート、検索を共有ランタイム信号で連動させる分散推論高速化フレームワークであり、推論サービングへの直接の貢献が確認できる
